To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the job’s motivating-potential, autonomy-supportive leaders, and understanding the company’s strategy are associated with job satisfaction, turnover intentions, and organizational citizenship behaviors (civic virtue and altruism).
intrinsic motivation and identified motivation are different motivational processes that are differentially associated with different work antecedents and different outcomes.

intrinsic motivation and identified motivation mediate the effects of job characteristics, autonomy support and organizational strategy on job satisfaction, turnover intentions and organizational citizenship behaviors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how the job’s motivating-potential, autonomy-supportive leaders, and understanding the strategy of one’s organization influence employee outcomes.
the question of how the job’s motivating characteristics, autonomy support, and strategy influence employees’ motivational processes and subsequent outcomes.
the impact of work design, autonomy support, and organizational strategy on employees’ motivational processes and their consequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self-determined motivational processes are more likely to occur and to have stronger effects in a work environment characterized by autonomy support and a clearly defined strategy.
the more self-determined an employee is, the more satisfied and engaged he or she is.
the motivational process of self-determination theory can be applied to the field of organizational behavior.
